title: Orchestrated readiness pauses for SLO stabilization
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem summary: During bursty traffic and partial infra degradation we observe autoscaler oscillation and cascading pod restarts that violate our latency and availability SLOs. Readiness/liveness probe flapping contributes to churn: short probe failures cause pods to be marked NotReady, triggering scale-downs and disruptive relocations. This ticket implements an "orchestrated readiness pause" mechanism plus safety circuit breaker rules to stabilize autoscaling decisions and enforce SLOs during transient degradations, while preserving multi-region failover semantics.

Goals:
- Introduce a coordinated readiness pause API and controller that can temporarily freeze readiness transitions for marked pods or groups (by region/role) for a bounded duration.
- Add a dynamic circuit breaker that gates aggressive scale-down when probe failure patterns match transient network/IO issues.
- Provide observability: dashboards and alerts that show pause events, autoscaler churn, and SLO impact.
- Ship runtime + k8s controller changes with a conservative rollout and rollback path, with a runbook for manual invocation during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes a namespaced CRD or API to request a readiness pause for a set of pods (region/cluster/label selector) with TTL
Paused pods do not flip readiness state for the TTL unless explicitly overridden by an emergency unpause
Autoscaler receives stabilized readiness signals and avoids scaling down nodes where more than X% of pods have transient failures (configurable), reducing churn by >= 40% in canary runs
Dashboards in Datadog show pause events, pause duration, autoscaler scale events, and a derived metric for "churn per minute"
Failover behavior: when an entire region is unhealthy, orchestrated pauses do not prevent multi-region failover (controller honors global failover policy)
Comprehensive unit/integration tests and a chaos simulation demonstrating improved SLO adherence under injected probe flaps
tasks: Design doc: outline CRD fields, TTL semantics, leader election and safety windows (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Orchestrated+Readiness+Pause )
Prototype controller: implement pause, unpause, and TTL enforcement (k8s controller + unit tests)
Runtime integration: add readiness pause hooks in the node agent and kube-proxy integration layer to ensure consistent signals
Circuit breaker rules: implement heuristic to de-rate scale-down when probe failure pattern matches transient classification (pattern matcher + metric window)
Observability: dashboards + alerts (Datadog) and log schema for pause events (link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts/readiness-pauses )
E2E tests: chaos experiments (packet loss, delayed storage ops) in the staging cluster using the sim-harness
Canary rollout plan: 10% of traffic in staging -> 1 region in prod -> progressive expansion with rollback threshold
Runbook: manual invocation steps, escalation path, and post-incident data collection template
